import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Subword complexity of the morphism a → aab, b → b

Let $a_n$ be the number of distinct subwords (contiguous factors) of length $n$ in the infinite
word generated by the morphism $\sigma: a \mapsto aab, b \mapsto b$, starting from $a$.
As shown in the references, $a_n$ is given by the formula
$$ a_n = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \min(2^i,n-i+1). $$

The conjectured generating function is:
$$\sum_{n \geq 0} a_n x^n = \frac{1}{1-x} + \frac{x}{(1-x)^2}\left(\frac{1}{1-x} -
  \sum_{k \geq 1} x^{2^k + k - 1}\right).$$

*References:*
- [A6697](https://oeis.org/A6697)
- J.-P. Allouche and J. Shallit, "On the subword complexity of the fixed point of a → aab, b → b,
  and generalizations," arXiv:1605.02361 [math.CO], 2016.
- N. J. A. Sloane and Simon Plouffe, *The Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences*, Academic Press, 1995.
-/

namespace OeisA6697

open PowerSeries WithPiTopology List

/-- The morphism σ on {a, b} defined by a ↦ aab, b ↦ b, represented on Bool where
`false` = a and `true` = b. -/
def morphism : Bool → List Bool
  | false => [false, false, true]  -- a ↦ aab
  | true => [true]                -- b ↦ b

/-- The n-th iterate of the morphism applied to [a]. -/
def finiteWord : ℕ → List Bool
  | 0 => [false]
  | n + 1 => (finiteWord n).flatMap morphism

@[simp, category API, AMS 68]
lemma count_false_morphism (b : Bool) : count false (morphism b) = if b then 0 else 2 := by
  cases b <;> simp [morphism]

@[simp, category API, AMS 68]
lemma count_true_morphism (b : Bool) : count true (morphism b) = 1 := by
  cases b <;> simp [morphism]

@[simp, category API, AMS 68]
lemma count_false_finiteWord : ∀ n, (finiteWord n).count false = 2 ^ n
  | 0 => rfl
  | n + 1 => by
    simp [finiteWord, count_flatMap, Function.comp_def, sum_map_ite, ← Bool.beq_eq_decide_eq,
      -beq_false, ← count_eq_length_filter, count_false_finiteWord, pow_succ]

@[simp, category API, AMS 68]
lemma count_true_finiteWord : ∀ n, (finiteWord n).count true = 2 ^ n - 1
  | 0 => rfl
  | n + 1 => by
    simp [finiteWord, List.count_flatMap, Function.comp_def, ← count_true_add_count_false,
      count_true_finiteWord, pow_succ]; omega

@[simp, category API, AMS 68]
lemma length_finiteWord (n : ℕ) : (finiteWord n).length = 2 ^ (n + 1) - 1 := by
  simp [← count_true_add_count_false, count_true_finiteWord, pow_succ]; omega

/-- The infinite word w is the fixed point of the morphism starting from 'a'.
We define it as the limit: w(i) is the i-th symbol, which stabilizes after
sufficiently many iterations. -/
noncomputable def infiniteWord (i : ℕ) : Bool :=
  (finiteWord (i + 1))[i]'(by grw [length_finiteWord, ← Nat.lt_two_pow_self] <;> lia)

/-- A subword (factor) of length n starting at position i. -/
noncomputable def subwordAt (i n : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (List.range n).map fun j => infiniteWord (i + j)

/-- The set of all distinct subwords of length n in the infinite word. -/
def subwordsOfLength (n : ℕ) : Set (List Bool) :=
  {w | ∃ i, w = subwordAt i n}

/-- The subword complexity function: a(n) is the number of distinct subwords of length n. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (subwordsOfLength n).ncard

/--
**Conjecture (A6697)**: The generating function for the number of subwords of length $n$
in the infinite word generated by $a \mapsto aab, b \mapsto b$ is
$$\sum_{n \geq 0} a_n x^n = 1 + \frac{1}{1-x} + \frac{1}{(1-x)^2}\left(\frac{1}{1-x} -
  \sum_{k \geq 0} x^{2^{k+1} + k}\right).$$

Equivalently, a(n) equals the n-th coefficient of this generating function.

However, the reference quoted in the OEIS sequence

> J.-P. Allouche and J. Shallit, "On the subword complexity of the fixed point of a → aab, b → b,
> and generalizations," arXiv:1605.02361 [math.CO], 2016.

provides an explicit formula
$$ a_n = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \min(2^i,n-i+1). $$

If one takes this as a definition of a(n) instead,
it becomes straightforward to prove the conjecture.
See https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/docs/OeisA6697.md
for a formal proof of the generating function using this definition.

Hence, a formalization of [arXiv:1605.02361](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02361)
would complete a formal proof as below.
-/
@[category research solved, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/OeisA6697/solution.lean", AMS 68]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) :
    a n = coeff (R := ℚ) n
      ((1 - X)⁻¹ + X * (1 - X)⁻¹ ^ 2 * ((1 - X)⁻¹ - ∑' k, X ^ (2 ^ (k + 1) + k))) := by
  sorry

end OeisA6697

findings.description: The generating function displayed in the theorem's docstring (lines 99–102) is not the one in the Lean statement. Writing S = ∑_{k≥0} x^(2^(k+1)+k), the docstring gives 1 + (1-x)^(-1) + (1-x)^(-2)((1-x)^(-1)-S), whereas Lean gives (1-x)^(-1) + x(1-x)^(-2)((1-x)^(-1)-S). Their constant coefficients are respectively 3 and 1, so the assertion that these are equivalent is incorrect. This error is inherited from the printed OEIS formula. The Lean identity itself is correct: it is equivalent to the finite-sum formula in the independently cited Allouche–Shallit paper.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A006697, Ralf Stephan's March 5, 2004 FORMULA entry, prints exactly the erroneous expression: 'G.f.: 1 + 1/(1-x) + 1/(1-x)^2 * [1/(1-x) - sum(k>=1, x^(2^k+k-1))] (conjectured).' Read through the official data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A006/A006697.seq. The entry has offset 0, its b-file starts '0 1', and Allouche–Shallit, https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02361, Theorem 1 and Table 1, give a(n)=∑_{i=0}^n min(2^i,n-i+1), including a(0)=1.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the correct Lean statement, but replace the displayed generating function in its docstring with the Lean formula: remove the leading 1 and insert the factor x before (1-x)^(-2). Explicitly describe this as a correction to the printed OEIS formula, or as an equivalent form of Allouche–Shallit Theorem 1, rather than claiming to prove the OEIS expression as printed.

status_issues.recorded: Unconditional formal_proof using lean4 at https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/OeisA6697/solution.lean, alongside category research solved.
status_issues.source_status: The cited Lean file proves the generating-function identity only for a sequence defined directly by the finite sum. It does not formally establish that this sequence equals the cardinality of the morphic word's factor set. Thus the link supplies the numerical part, not a complete formal proof of this declaration. The research solved category is nevertheless justified by Allouche–Shallit's 2016 mathematical proof.
status_issues.evidence: In the exact linked solution, lines 11–13 define a n := ∑ i ∈ range (n+1), min (2^i) (n-i+1), and the final conjecture theorem uses that definition. The entire file imports only Mathlib and contains no morphism, factor-cardinality definition, or bridge theorem. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/main/OeisA6697/solution.lean. The reviewed file's own lines 117–118 also acknowledge that formalizing the paper would complete the formal proof.

reformulations.difference: Instead of defining the infinite word by a limit of morphism iterates, Lean takes its ith symbol from finiteWord (i+1).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The morphism preserves prefixes, and finiteWord n is a prefix of finiteWord (n+1). Consequently, whenever an iterate contains position i, its symbol there agrees with every longer iterate. The proved length formula ensures that finiteWord (i+1) contains position i. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved prefix compatibility and the precise equivalence infiniteWord i = b ↔ ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, (finiteWord n)[i]? = some b. Thus this definition is exactly the coordinatewise stabilized limit used by the paper.

reformulations.difference: Relative to Allouche–Shallit Theorem 1, Lean states a rational power-series coefficient identity rather than a(n)=∑_{i=0}^n min(2^i,n-i+1). This equivalence is with the paper's formula, not with the erroneous OEIS generating function quoted in the docstring.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The nth coefficient of the actual Lean right-hand side is ∑_{i=0}^n min(2^i,n-i+1). Algebraically, summing the finite-sum formula gives (1-x)^(-2)∑_{i≥0}x^i(1-x^(2^i)); separating i=0 and reindexing the remaining sparse series yields the Lean expression. In /workspace/review/equivalence.lean I verified the linked numerical identity after a compatibility port, then proved for every b : ℕ → ℕ that the coefficient identity for all n is equivalent to b(n)=∑_{i=0}^n min(2^i,n-i+1) for all n. Specializing to OeisA6697.a gives the desired ↔. Coercion to ℚ is injective, and coefficientwise equality is equivalent to equality of formal power series. These proofs do not use OeisA6697.conjecture and have no sorryAx dependency.

https://neilsloane.com/doc/books.html — bibliographic entry for the 1995 Encyclopedia
review.notes: All six definitions, five API lemmas, and the problem theorem were checked. No mathematical defect was found in the Lean definitions or theorem statement. Scratch proofs establish finiteness and nonemptiness of every factor set, a(0)=1, a(1)=2, a(2)=4, stabilization of the word, summability of the sparse power series, and the unequal constant coefficients of the two displayed formulas. The inverse of 1-X is a genuine unit inverse, and Set.ncard's infinite-set default is unreachable. Finite-iterate factor counts match the initial sequence values; an independent computation checked the finite-sum formula against all 1001 b-file entries. The external numerical proof compiles without sorryAx after replacing one outdated topology-API proof step; that compatibility issue is not reported as a defect. OEIS HTML was blocked, so its official data mirror was used. The 1995 book was located bibliographically but not inspected; the primary 2016 paper fully specifies the relevant mathematics. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; the target file still matches its committed blob.
